artists.biography:
The Future Sound of London (often abbreviated to FSOL) is a British electronic music band composed of Garry Cobain (sometimes styled as Gaz Cobain) and Brian Dougans. The duo are often credited with pushing the boundaries of electronic music experimentation and of pioneering a new era of dance music. Although often labelled as ambient, Cobain and Dougans usually resist being typecast into any one particular genre. Their work covers most areas of electronic music, such as ambient techno, house music, trip-hop, ambient dub, acid techno and often involves extreme experimentation; for example they have, since the turn of the millennium, experimented with psychedelic rock under their Amorphous Androgynous alias. In addition to music composition, their interests have covered a number of areas including film and video, 2D and 3D computer graphics, animation in making almost all their own videos for their singles, radio broadcasting and creating their own electronic devices for sound making. They have released works under numerous aliases.
The artists have been fairly enigmatic in the past but have become more candid with their fanbase in recent years with social websites like Myspace, Youtube, their forum and many interviews in which Cobain almost always speaks for the group.

perplexity.description:
Dead Cities is the third studio album by British electronic duo The Future Sound of London, originally released in October 1996 through Virgin Records. The album is a landmark in experimental electronic music, blending ambient textures, breakbeats, and cinematic soundscapes. Its style is characterized by a fusion of atmospheric drones, fragmented rhythms, and subtle melodic motifs, creating a sense of urban decay and technological unease. The record marked a shift from the more accessible dance-oriented sound of their earlier work toward a more abstract and immersive approach.

Within the band's discography, Dead Cities stands as a pivotal release, bridging their earlier club-focused material with the increasingly psychedelic and genre-defying direction they would pursue on subsequent albums like The Isness. The album's final track, "Dead Cities Reprise," foreshadows the expansive, organic soundscapes that would define their later output. Commercially, Dead Cities reached No. 26 on the UK Albums Chart and No. 2 on the UK Dance Albums Chart, while singles "My Kingdom" and "We Have Explosive" both charted in the UK Top 15. The album was widely praised for its innovative production and atmospheric depth, cementing The Future Sound of London's reputation as pioneers of electronic music.
